editorial:
Imagine being a young woman in 1800s France with a huge heart but a personality that just won't quit. You meet Leonie, a girl from a wealthy family who wants to dedicate her life to God, but she has a bit of a temper and a stubborn streak. Her mother is constantly stressed out, and the nuns at the monasteries she tries to join are totally overwhelmed by her. It is a slow-burn family drama that feels like stepping back in time, focusing on the struggle between wanting to be a good person and fighting your own natural instincts.

The acting is solid, and the period costumes look great, though the pace is definitely on the slower side. If you enjoy character studies about faith and growth, you will really dig this. It is not an action movie, so be ready for lots of talking and emotional tension.
endingExplained: After a long struggle with her pride and anger, Leonie finally finds a sense of peace and purpose. She learns to control her difficult nature and accepts the discipline of the religious life. The movie wraps up with her finding a place where she truly fits in, showing that her journey was less about the monastery and more about fixing her own heart. She ends the story as a changed, calmer woman.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about personal growth.
